_: M45b actor seed. Actor is global; vision/capability assignments are per-vision M2M joins. Adding entries here populates the Hero Actors band + capability card 'Active actors' footer + /visions/[slug]/actors/[key] detail pages. Signal extractor agent (M39+M45b) matches Signal.actor_id against actor.signal_keywords per-vision when confidence > 0.8.

actors.name: SpaceX
actors.blurb: Cheap launch + Starship — sets the orbital DC capex floor.
actors.description: SpaceX operates Falcon 9 (reusable medium-lift) and is developing Starship (super-heavy, fully reusable). Its $/kg-to-LEO curve is the primary cost lever for orbital data centers.

actors.name: Lonestar Data Holdings
actors.blurb: Orbital DC payload startup; Series B 2026.
actors.description: First-mover commercial orbital DC operator; lunar + LEO demos planned for 2027.

actors.name: Starcloud
actors.blurb: 1kW orbital heat-rejection demo (2025); scaling to 100kW.
actors.description: Early-stage in-orbit thermal radiator demonstrator. Only commercial actor with proven in-orbit thermal demo at meaningful scale.

actors.name: Advanced Micro Devices
actors.blurb: GPU competitor; MI300 rad-qual in flight.
actors.description: GPU and CPU manufacturer pursuing radiation qualification of the MI300 family at NASA Pegasus. Outcome gates orbital training workloads.

actors.name: NVIDIA
actors.blurb: Dominant ground GPU player; orbital rad-tolerance roadmap pending.
actors.description: Dominant AI accelerator supplier. Orbital rad-tolerance announcement would materially shift the binding capability.

actors.name: Intel
actors.blurb: Foundry + accelerator competitor; rad-hard SoC programs.
actors.description: Intel Foundry Services + Gaudi/Ponte Vecchio accelerator lines. Some rad-hard SoC work via Altera.

actors.name: Cobham Microelectronics
actors.blurb: Radiation-hardened microelectronics specialist.
actors.description: Lead supplier of rad-hard ICs, FPGAs, and memory to space programs. The default vendor for rad-tolerant logic.

actors.name: Mynaric
actors.blurb: Optical comms terminals — Tbps-class downlink shipping.
actors.description: Volume optical terminal supplier; lead actor on downlink capability.

actors.name: NASA
actors.blurb: OSAM-1 assembly + Pegasus rad-qual facility.
actors.description: Anchor lab for in-orbit assembly + radiation testing. OSAM-1 demonstrator delays directly affect assembly score.

actors.name: European Space Agency
actors.blurb: Optical comms + radiator R&D + payload programs.
actors.description: Active across downlink + thermal capabilities; lab-scale demos feed commercial pipeline.

actors.name: Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency
actors.blurb: Optical comms milestone partner.
actors.description: Active on optical downlink demonstrations; Hayabusa heritage useful for in-orbit thermal.

actors.name: Jet Propulsion Laboratory
actors.blurb: Thermal control flagship lab.
actors.description: Caltech-operated FFRDC. Long history of in-orbit thermal control technology development.

actors.name: Redwire Space (Made In Space)
actors.blurb: In-orbit manufacturing + assembly competitor to OSAM-1.
actors.description: Acquired Made In Space; pursues commercial OSAM (on-orbit servicing, assembly, manufacturing).

actors.name: Northrop Grumman
actors.blurb: MEV satellite servicing competitor.
actors.description: Operates MEV (Mission Extension Vehicle) servicing program. Adjacent to in-orbit assembly capability.

actors.name: Lloyd's of London
actors.blurb: Orbital insurance market hub — $2B/y aggregate cap.
actors.description: Insurance market that underwrites the majority of orbital programs. Underwriting depth caps project size.

actors.name: AXA XL Space Insurance
actors.blurb: Second-tier orbital underwriter.
actors.description: Continental European orbital insurance carrier; rare among non-Lloyd's writers.

actors.name: International Telecommunication Union
actors.blurb: Spectrum coordination for Ka/Q-band orbital links.
actors.description: UN body that allocates orbital spectrum + slots. Ka/Q-band largely settled; per-constellation coordination ongoing.

actors.name: US Federal Communications Commission
actors.blurb: US spectrum + orbital licensing regulator.
actors.description: Issues US spectrum licenses + orbital debris mitigation rules.

actors.name: Uptime Institute
actors.blurb: Tier-N reliability certification authority for data centers.
actors.description: Sets Tier-I through Tier-IV reliability standards for terrestrial DCs; orbital adaptation pending.

actors.name: SolAero Technologies
actors.blurb: Space-grade solar cells (acquired by Rocket Lab).
actors.description: Premier US space solar cell manufacturer; now part of Rocket Lab.

actors.name: Maxar Technologies
actors.blurb: Satellite buses + Earth observation incumbent.
actors.description: Largest US commercial satellite bus supplier. Power systems + integration depth.

actors.name: Rocket Lab
actors.blurb: Small-lift competitor; Neutron medium-lift in development.
actors.description: Electron (small-lift) operational; Neutron under development as a medium-lift reusable competitor.

actors.name: Blue Origin
actors.blurb: New Glenn heavy-lift competitor.
actors.description: New Glenn heavy-lift reusable; lunar Blue Moon lander program.

actors.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems
actors.blurb: SPARC tokamak; HTS magnet breakthrough (2021) revived private fusion.
actors.description: MIT PSFC spinout. Building SPARC (140 MW thermal, Q > 10) in Devens, MA; targets first plasma 2026. ARC commercial follow-on planned 2030s.

actors.name: Helion Energy
actors.blurb: D-He3 pulsed FRC plant; Microsoft PPA 2028.
actors.description: Pulsed magneto-inertial fusion using D-He3 reactions. Microsoft signed 50 MW PPA for 2028 delivery — most aggressive commercial timeline.

actors.name: TAE Technologies
actors.blurb: FRC + boron fuel; longest-running private fusion company.
actors.description: Field-reversed configuration with p-B11 aneutronic fuel ambition. Norman device sustained 30M+ K plasmas; Copernicus next.

actors.name: Tokamak Energy
actors.blurb: Spherical tokamak with HTS magnets; ST40 Q-test 2026.
actors.description: UK spherical tokamak company. ST40 achieved 100M K plasma 2022; ST80-HTS planned 2026.

actors.name: General Fusion
actors.blurb: Magnetized target fusion; LM26 demo in Vancouver.
actors.description: Canadian MTF approach using liquid lithium vortex + plasma compression. LM26 demo plant under construction at Culham, UK.

actors.name: ITER Organization
actors.blurb: 500 MW intergovernmental tokamak; first plasma slipped to 2035.
actors.description: International collaboration (EU, US, JP, KR, CN, IN, RU). Cadarache site. Q > 10 demonstrator. TBM test blanket modules expected 2035+.

actors.name: Lawrence Livermore — NIF
actors.blurb: NIF achieved Q > 1 inertial confinement, Dec 2022.
actors.description: National Ignition Facility. Laser-driven inertial confinement. First repeated Q > 1 ignition shots 2022-24 — proved net energy gain is physically possible.

actors.name: MIT Plasma Science & Fusion Center
actors.blurb: Academic anchor; HTS magnet test bed; CFS parent.
actors.description: Spawned CFS via SPARC concept. Test cell for high-field magnets. Workforce pipeline for US private fusion.

actors.name: KSTAR (Korea)
actors.blurb: Daejeon tokamak; 100M K sustained 48s record (2024).
actors.description: Korea Superconducting Tokamak Advanced Research. Operated by KFE. Holds duration record for >100M K plasma.

actors.name: UK Atomic Energy Authority
actors.blurb: JET legacy + STEP prototype targeting 2040.
actors.description: Operates JET (decommissioning 2024); leads STEP (Spherical Tokamak for Energy Production) prototype targeting net power by 2040.

actors.name: US DOE Fusion Energy Sciences
actors.blurb: Primary US fusion R&D funder; Milestone-Based Program 2023.
actors.description: Office of Science FES program. Funded $46M Milestone-Based Fusion Development across 8 private companies in 2023.

actors.name: US Nuclear Regulatory Commission
actors.blurb: April 2024 ruling: fusion under Part 30 byproduct material framework.
actors.description: Issued landmark fusion-regulatory framework decision April 2024 — fusion plants licensed as byproduct material, not Part 50 reactors. Order-of-magnitude faster licensing.

actors.name: Faraday Factory Japan
actors.blurb: REBCO HTS tape producer; supplies CFS + Tokamak Energy.
actors.description: Japan-based REBCO tape manufacturer. Doubling capacity 2024-26 to meet fusion demand.

actors.name: American Superconductor
actors.blurb: US REBCO supplier; DOE-funded capacity expansion 2024.
actors.description: Public US superconductor company. REBCO tape products supply fusion + grid + utility customers. DOE awards 2024 expand domestic capacity.

actors.name: SK hynix
actors.blurb: HBM market leader; M16 fab + HBM3E 12-Hi yield ramp.
actors.description: Korean memory maker; dominant HBM3E supplier to NVIDIA training clusters. M16-2 capacity build-out runs through 2027.

actors.name: Samsung Semiconductor
actors.blurb: HBM3E qualification race + pyeongtaek HBM capex.
actors.description: Largest Korean memory maker. HBM3E qualification with second-tier accelerator partner extends supplier mix. Pyeongtaek expansion targets share recovery.

actors.name: Micron Technology
actors.blurb: US incumbent; 1-gamma node + HBM capex pivot.
actors.description: Only US-headquartered DRAM major. Node migration to 1-gamma + capex reallocation toward HBM mix is the durability story.

actors.name: NVIDIA
actors.blurb: HBM consumer-of-record; multi-vendor qualification driver.
actors.description: Largest HBM customer worldwide. Multi-vendor HBM4 qualification is the lever that splits pricing power between SK hynix / Samsung / Micron.

actors.name: TSMC
actors.blurb: Foundry leader; CoWoS packaging is the HBM bottleneck.
actors.description: Taiwan foundry. CoWoS advanced packaging capacity gates how many HBM-stacked accelerators ship per quarter.

actors.name: Intel
actors.blurb: Foundry pivot; Gaudi accelerator HBM qualifier.
actors.description: Intel Foundry Services + Gaudi accelerator portfolio re-enters the HBM consumer pool from a different angle than NVIDIA.

actors.name: AMD
actors.blurb: MI300 / MI400 HBM consumer; share-vs-NVIDIA wedge.
actors.description: Instinct MI300/MI400 demand is the second-largest HBM call after NVIDIA. Share gains compound HBM ASP durability.

actors.name: Kioxia
actors.blurb: NAND-side counterweight; HBM-adjacent flash story.
actors.description: Japanese flash major (formerly Toshiba Memory). HBM-adjacent: tighter NAND market raises the relative attractiveness of HBM-focused capex.

actors.name: ASML
actors.blurb: EUV monopoly; node-migration enabler.
actors.description: Sole EUV lithography supplier. Tool deliveries gate Korean + US fabs' node-migration cadence.

actors.name: US Bureau of Industry and Security
actors.blurb: Sets US export controls — HBM licensing pivot.
actors.description: BIS export-license framework controls HBM shipments to China-listed entities. Rule updates shift TAM materially.

actors.name: Semiconductor Industry Association
actors.blurb: Industry policy + monthly billings authority.
actors.description: US industry body. Monthly billings releases are the cleanest demand-side leading indicator for the memory cycle.

actors.name: Bloom Energy
actors.blurb: Largest commercial SOFC OEM; AI-DC offtake leader.
actors.description: US public SOFC manufacturer. Hyperscaler offtake announcements + Fremont expansion are the binding signal for behind-the-meter deployments.

actors.name: Doosan Fuel Cell
actors.blurb: Korean SOFC market leader; municipal + SE Asia exports.
actors.description: Korean public SOFC manufacturer. Domestic municipal contracts + SE Asia export ramp anchor the Asia-side story.

actors.name: Ceres Power
actors.blurb: Asset-light licensee model; Bosch + Doosan partners.
actors.description: UK SOFC IP licensor (steel-cell stack design). Licensee revenue (Bosch, Doosan, Weichai) is the durability story.

actors.name: FuelCell Energy
actors.blurb: MCFC pivot; DOE-funded SOFC tech path.
actors.description: US public fuel-cell company. SOFC R&D + carbon-capture program runs alongside the molten-carbonate (MCFC) commercial base.

actors.name: Mitsubishi Power
actors.blurb: Hybrid SOFC-GT systems for industrial / DC.
actors.description: MHI subsidiary. SOFC-gas-turbine hybrid systems target industrial + large-scale DC behind-the-meter use cases.

actors.name: Convion
actors.blurb: EU SOFC system integrator; biogas + H2 ready.
actors.description: Finnish SOFC integrator. Fuel-flex stack designs target biogas + green-H2 hybrid markets.

actors.name: Sunfire
actors.blurb: Reversible SOFC / electrolyzer; green-H2 bridge.
actors.description: German SOFC + SOE company. Reversible stack design ties SOFC commercial path directly to EU green-H2 buildout.

actors.name: SOLIDpower
actors.blurb: EU residential / light-commercial SOFC modules.
actors.description: Italian SOFC module maker. Residential + light-commercial deployments across EU give a different denominator vs hyperscaler-DC use.

actors.name: US DOE — EERE Fuel Cells
actors.blurb: H2Hubs program + stack-cost-down funding.
actors.description: DOE Office of Energy Efficiency & Renewable Energy. H2Hubs + stack-cost-down funding directly subsidizes SOFC OEM bill of materials.
signal_keywords: Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Technologies Office

actors.name: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
actors.blurb: Interconnection-queue rulemaking authority.
actors.description: US FERC. Queue-reform orders shorten the interconnection wait for behind-the-meter SOFC by months → meaningful LCOE accretion.

actors.name: International Energy Agency
actors.blurb: Authoritative LCOE + H2 cost curve outlook.
actors.description: IEA technical reports on SOFC system cost + green-H2 production cost are the reference outlook investors price against.
